result.rationale: Verified: poll_feed.rb takes `i.content` from the feed and passes to TopicEmbed.import, which creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`; Post#cook then does `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, bypassing the sanitizing cooking pipeline. The embed view renders `raw post.cooked`, so injected scripts/handlers from the feed would execute under the forum's origin. This is a genuine, verifiable security defect introduced by this diff.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows in poll_feed.rb line 35: `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` followed by `TopicEmbed.import(user, url, i.title, content)`. In topic_embed.rb, the import method uses `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` which bypasses cooking/sanitization (as shown in post.rb lines 131-133: `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`). The ruby-readability library in import_remote only allows specific tags but the poll_feed path directly imports RSS content without such filtering. This means malicious RSS feed content with scripts or event handlers would be rendered as raw HTML without sanitization.
